title: Efficacy and safety of more intensive lowering of LDL cholesterol: a meta-analysis of data from 170,000 participants in 26 randomised trials
authors: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' (CTT) Collaboration, Baigent C, Blackwell L, Emberson J, Holland LE, Reith C, et al.
followUp: median 4.8 years in trials of statin against control; 5.1 years in trials of more against less intensive statin
population: Individual participant data from 21 randomised trials of statin against control (129,526 participants) and 5 trials of more against less intensive statin regimens (39,612 participants), each with at least 1000 participants and 2 years of scheduled treatment
funder: This work is supported at the CTSU by the UK Medical Research Council, British Heart Foundation, and, previously, the European Community Biomed Programme, and at the CTC by the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council and National Heart Foundation. The funding sources had no involvement in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, report writing or publication.
authorConflicts: Most of the trials in this report were supported by research grants from the pharmaceutical industry. Some members of the writing committee received reimbursement of costs of scientific meetings from the pharmaceutical industry; two received honoraria from Solvay. The membership list names representatives of Bristol-Myers Squibb, Merck, Laboratoires Fournier, Bayer, Novartis Pharma, AstraZeneca and Pfizer as observers, and states that all collaborators had an opportunity to contribute to interpretation and drafting.
result: In the 21 trials of statin against control, first major vascular events (major coronary event, coronary revascularisation or stroke) occurred in 7136 (2.8% per annum) of 64,744 participants allocated statin against 8934 (3.6% per annum) of 64,782 allocated control, a 22% (95% CI 19 to 24) reduction with a weighted mean LDL cholesterol difference of 1.07 mmol/L at 1 year; 21% (19 to 23) per 1.0 mmol/L. Across all 26 trials, per 1.0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction: major vascular events rate ratio 0.78 (0.76 to 0.80); all-cause mortality 0.90 (0.87 to 0.93); cancer incidence 1.00 (0.96 to 1.04). Excess rhabdomyolysis 1 (SE 1) per 10,000 in the trials of statin against control.
